entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Monte Cassino was a pivotal assault by the Allies against the Axis forces' winter line in Italy, held from December 1943 to May 1944. This brutal and bloody campaign, fought in the heart of Southern Europe, would ultimately determine the fate of World War II in the region. The battle raged on for five months, with Allied forces launching repeated attacks against the heavily fortified German positions, inflicting heavy casualties on both sides.

The German resistance, led by General Heinrich von Vietinghoff, held out for an astonishing 154 days, but ultimately succumbed to the relentless Allied pressure. The breakthrough came on May 18, 1944, when the Allies finally breached the German defenses, marking a decisive victory in the Italian Campaign.

The legacy of the Battle of Monte Cassino was profound. It paved the way for the Allied advance into Italy, marking a crucial turning point in the war. The battle also showcased the tenacity and bravery of Allied forces, as well as the determination of the German military to hold out against overwhelming odds. The costly and bloody conflict would leave an indelible mark on the region, shaping the course of European history for generations to come.

The cost of the battle was staggering. Over 55,000 Allied troops were killed or wounded, with an estimated 20,000 German soldiers also losing their lives. The destruction of the medieval monastery at Monte Cassino, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was particularly devastating, with the iconic building reduced to rubble in the final stages of the battle.
